correctness.rationale: Pinching into accepted and rejected blocks is trace-distance contractive. Each block has trace imbalance of magnitude \(d=|p-q|\), giving a \(d/2\) trace-norm contribution. If \(p\ge q\), the triangle inequality applied to \(p(\rho_P-\sigma_P)=(p\rho_P-q\sigma_P)-(p-q)\sigma_P\) gives \(\delta_P\ge pc-d/2\). Therefore \(D(\rho,\sigma)\ge\max\{d,pc\}\), with the symmetric case obtained by interchange. The three-level diagonal family evaluates exactly to \(D(\rho,\sigma)=\max\{d,pc\}\), proving sharpness. Random matrix checks and equality-family checks were replayed from the packaged checker.

value.rationale: The result gives the exact worst-case stability constant for the postselection step used in a new finite-measurement quantum-state certification theorem. It removes a mismatch penalty from the current public bound, identifies the larger acceptance probability as the sole amplification denominator, and proves all-parameter optimality. At the minimal feasible global distance \(\tau=|p-q|\), it also quantifies how much conditional-state change can be hidden entirely inside acceptance imbalance. This is a structural boundary result with direct use in finite-noise budgeting rather than a parameter substitution or numerical increment.
